hero.eyebrow: President, Council of the African Space Agency
hero.title: Steering Africa's sovereign presence in the space domain
hero.bio: H.E. Dr. Tidiane Ouattara is a distinguished African space leader, strategist, and international advocate for science, technology, and innovation. He is the elected President of the Council of the African Space Agency and has held senior leadership roles at the Canadian Space Agency and the African Union Commission.

about.label: About
about.heading: Architect of Africa's Space Sovereignty
about.p1: H.E. Dr. Tidiane Ouattara is the elected President of the Council of the African Space Agency. A space scientist with a PhD in Remote Sensing and GIS from Université de Sherbrooke (Canada), he has built a 29-year career at the intersection of space science, policy, and international diplomacy — holding senior leadership roles at the Canadian Space Agency, Natural Resources Canada, Environment and Climate Change Canada, and the African Union Commission.
about.p2: He has mobilised over US $155M for African space and Earth observation programmes, led the GMES & Africa initiative across 45 countries, and driven the ratification of the African Space Policy and Strategy by all 55 AU member states. His work bridges science and diplomacy, forging international partnerships that translate space knowledge into agricultural resilience, disaster preparedness, and climate action for African communities.
about.quote: Space is not a luxury for Africa. It is infrastructure — as essential as roads, as vital as water.

experience.label: Career Highlights
experience.heading: A Lifetime of Strategic Leadership
experience.bio: H.E. Dr. Tidiane Ouattara holds a PhD and a Master's degree in Remote Sensing and Geographical Information Systems from Université de Sherbrooke (Canada) and a Master's in Physical Geography from Université Cocody-Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire). He is the elected President of the Council of the African Space Agency. Over a 29-year career spanning academia, the private sector, and public service, he has held leadership positions at the Canadian Space Agency, Natural Resources Canada, Environment and Climate Change Canada, and the African Union Commission. He has mobilised over US $155M for space and Earth observation programmes and has represented Africa at every major international space governance forum.
experience.e1_role: President, Council of the African Space Agency
experience.e1_desc: Elected by the African Union Assembly to lead the governance of AfSA, the first continental space body with 156 permanent positions and an annual budget exceeding US $5M. Responsibilities include ensuring good governance, leading the African space programme, mobilising member states and strategic partners, negotiating resources, and promoting international partnerships.
experience.e1_achievements: Key achievements: operationalised the Agency with its official opening before 500+ guests; began staff recruitment, infrastructure acquisition, and first programme implementation; negotiated a €100M European Commission investment in the Global Gateway space component — Phase 1 (Africa–Europe Space Partnership Programme) of €45M launched January 2025; initiated and signed partnership agreements with ESA, EUMETSAT, EU Joint Research Centre, NASA, NOAA, CNSA, JAXA, ISRO, ROSCOMOS, AEB, UAESA, and numerous international financial institutions.
experience.e2_role: Interim Director — STI / Head of Division — Science, Technology & Space
experience.e2_org: African Union Commission — Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
experience.e2_desc: Coordinated space science and policy initiatives across the AU Commission. Integrated space science and its applications into socioeconomic development strategies. Developed and implemented space programmes including the GMES & Africa Programme and the Africa–Europe Space Partnership.
experience.e2_achievements: Key achievements: developed and implemented the African Outer Space Programme centred on Earth Observation, satellite communications, navigation and positioning, and astronomy and space science across 9 years; drafted the African Space Policy and Strategy ratified by all 55 member states; secured consensus and elaborated common African positions on space policy and programme issues; organised the first Africa–Europe Space Policy Dialogue in Dakar (2022); led the creation and operationalisation of AfSA with a 156-position structure approved by Heads of State; successfully implemented two phases of the GMES & Africa Programme (€55M) involving 170+ institutions across 45 African countries — training 15,000 professionals and students, awarding 20 grants (€35M+) and 46 scholarships, equipping 11 countries with satellite data reception stations, and establishing the Women in GMES network (250+ members) and the GMES & Africa Academic Network (40+ universities, 120+ faculty).
experience.e3_role: Head Manager — Geospatial Data Management & Ecosystem Assessment
experience.e3_org: Environment and Climate Change Canada — Canadian Wildlife Service
experience.e3_desc: Led Earth observation and geospatial data management initiatives. Provided national leadership in applying geomatics to landscape assessment and wildlife habitat conservation planning. Developed the geospatial component of Canada's National Conservation Plan.
experience.e3_achievements: Key achievements: created and chaired the CWS Data Management Committee and Working Group; authored the CWS Sensitive Data Publication Policy and the Unit's Integrated Business Plan; managed 16 employees with a budget of CAD $1.2M+ including salaries, grants and contributions, and O&M.
experience.e4_role: Manager — Landscape and Protected Areas Policy & Planning
experience.e4_desc: Built a fully operational Policy and Planning Section from 25% to 100% staffing (20 employees) in six months. Designed and implemented the section's first integrated strategic business plan covering a budget of CAD $3.3M+ including salaries, grants/contributions (CAD $1.5M), and O&M. Led national programme coordination across Environment Canada's regional offices and with other departments.
experience.e5_role: Manager — Canadian Digital Elevation Model Programme
experience.e5_org: Natural Resources Canada — Earth Science Sector
experience.e5_desc: Managed the Canadian Digital Elevation Data (CDED) project under GEOBASE and the Limited Access Road project under the Topographic Map Revision Initiative. Revitalised the CDED project by securing buy-in and partnerships with provincial governments, NGOs, and academia. Conducted SWOT analysis. Led collective staffing activities for the Mapping Directorate.
experience.e6_role: Head — Knowledge Management, Bilateral & Multilateral Strategies
experience.e6_org: Natural Resources Canada — Science and Policy Integration
experience.e6_desc: Developed the integrated knowledge management business plan and provided strategic advice on NRCan's bilateral and multilateral strategies in natural resources. Established strategic direction for the new Knowledge Management Strategy Unit.
experience.e7_org: Natural Resources Canada — Office of the Chief Scientist
experience.e7_desc: Provided strategic S&T policy advice to the Chief Scientist and Assistant Deputy Minister. Led the concept and development of NRCan's S&T Strategy prospectus covering priority-setting, governance, capacity-building, collaboration, and stakeholder engagement. Analysed S&T policy across 9 innovative countries (France, UK, US, China, Japan, Norway, Finland, Australia, New Zealand).
experience.e8_desc: Provided strategic advice to senior management and the CSA Executive Committee on international space policy. Developed the first CSA Strategic Framework for Earth Observation in Africa and MoUs with the Argentine Space Agency and Egypt's NARSS. Led the Canadian delegation to UNCOPUOS for two years. Conducted scientific and commercial missions to Egypt, Algeria, and South Africa.
experience.e9_desc: Developed an expert system for landslide monitoring and a remote sensing/GIS methodology for rapid change detection. Authored NRCan's first Geomatics Strategy for Africa. Led scientific and commercial missions to Gabon, Senegal, Kenya, and Ethiopia. Negotiated partnership agreements with key African geomatics organisations including the Centre de Suivi Écologique du Sénégal and the Regional Centre for Mapping of Resources for Development (Kenya).
experience.e10_desc: Strengthened scientific and technical capacity of researchers at INERA in Earth observation and GIS for sustainable development. Automated horticulture mapping using remote sensing in Montérégie for GEOMAT International.
experience.e11_desc: Taught undergraduate courses in hydrology, Earth observation (satellite image processing and analysis), geopolitics and geography of Africa, climatology and hydrometeorology, GIS, and geographical methods and techniques. Developed an original remote sensing approach for land-cover and land-use change estimation and a new water erosion model for high-relief semi-arid regions using satellite imagery. Published multiple scientific papers.

timeline.t1_role: President, Council of the African Space Agency
timeline.t1_desc: Elected by the African Union Assembly as the inaugural President of the AfSA Council. Leading the operationalisation of the Agency — including the build-out of its headquarters, the recruitment of 156 permanent staff, and the negotiation of strategic partnerships with ESA, NASA, JAXA, ISRO, and CNSA.
timeline.t2_desc: Led the development and implementation of the African Outer Space Programme and the GMES & Africa Programme (€55M). Drove the ratification of the African Space Policy and Strategy by all 55 member states. Mobilised over €100M in investment, including the Africa–Europe Space Partnership Programme.
timeline.t3_desc: Led geospatial data management and ecosystem assessment planning for the Canadian Wildlife Service. Developed the geospatial component of Canada's National Conservation Plan. Managed teams of 20 staff and a budget of over CAD $3M.
timeline.t4_desc: Managed international space policy portfolios covering Earth Observation, Navigation, Robotics, and Space Sciences for Africa, the Americas, and the United Nations. Led the Canadian delegation to UNCOPUOS.
timeline.t5_role: PhD in Remote Sensing & GIS / Lecturer
timeline.t5_desc: Earned a PhD in Remote Sensing and Geographical Information Systems. Taught courses in hydrology, satellite image analysis, GIS, and climatology. Published peer-reviewed research on erosion modelling in semi-arid environments.

sheets.ev1_title: UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space
sheets.ev1_desc: Keynote address on behalf of the African Union at COPUOS, presenting the AfSA mandate and advocating for equitable access to orbital slots for developing nations.
sheets.ev2_title: African Union Summit Side Event — Space Policy Dialogue
sheets.ev2_desc: Hosted a high-level ministerial dialogue on harmonising Africa's national space legislations with the continental Space Policy and Strategy framework.
sheets.ev3_desc: Chaired the inaugural Africa Space Pavilion at IAC 2024, spotlighting breakthroughs from AfSA member states and facilitating investment conversations with commercial operators.
sheets.ev4_desc: Opening ceremony address; announced the AfSA Young Innovators in Space grant programme for sub-Saharan universities. Moderated a panel on NewSpace startups on the continent.
sheets.ev5_desc: Concluded a landmark Cooperation Agreement with ESA covering Earth Observation data sharing, joint training programs, and co-development of the Africa Environmental Monitoring satellite constellation.
sheets.ev6_desc: Invited address on "Space as the Fourth Industrial Revolution for Africa," moderated discussion with heads of state and global technology CEOs on space investment in emerging markets.
